interactions.teaches: A large number of repeaters can still amount to only a small number of actual origins.
interactions.studentAction: Trace the network backward through four labeled stages.
interactions.feedback: The crowd of reports reduces to reprints, then two Michigan events, while a distinct-origin counter falls without hiding any step.
interactions.staticFallback: All four stages render as a readable sequence with their counts.
interactions.identityFit: A tuning needle moving backward through a signal chain belongs to the receiver-and-frequency register.

interactions.teaches: Independent source count depends on origin, not the number of people repeating a statement.
interactions.studentAction: Switch between a rumor claim and a Watergate claim, then group statements by where they came from.
interactions.feedback: The rumor stack collapses to one shared origin while the documented claim retains independently failing records or witnesses.
interactions.staticFallback: Both grouped cases remain visible as labeled tables.
interactions.identityFit: The readout tunes out duplicate signals and locks only distinct origins.

interactions.teaches: A claim is checkable only when disconfirming evidence could change the conclusion.
interactions.studentAction: Open the same three questions for the rumor and the Watergate case.
interactions.feedback: Each case reveals what would end the claim, whether that evidence existed, and whether the claim was held so the evidence could matter.
interactions.staticFallback: Both complete three-field records render in a comparison table.
interactions.identityFit: The same fixed test is tuned to two different signals, keeping the procedure neutral.
